title: Flood Advisory
location: Madison, IL

details.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Madison County in southwestern Illinois...

* WHEN...Until noon CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

Carpenter, Hamel, Pierron, Grantfork, New Douglas, Kaufman, Fruit
and Kuhn.

details.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 103 expected.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Iowa, southwest
Minnesota, and east central and southeast South Dakota.

* WHEN...From noon today to 8 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
details.instruction:
Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

title: Flood Warning
location: Live Oak, TX

details.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 1.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday morning and continue rising to 40.4 feet Thursday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 40.6
feet on 07/11/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

evening.

feet on 09/18/2002.

title: Flood Warning
location: Dimmit, TX

details.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.

* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding reaches into low
lying areas of the flood plain. Livestock should be moved from
vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 23.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 7:30 AM CDT Saturday was 25.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
late this evening and continue falling to 9.7 feet Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
23.5 feet on 07/27/1992.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight by 230 AM CDT.

location: Northern Black Hills; Central Black Hills; Southern Black Hills; Fall River County Area; Northern Foot Hills; Eastern Foot Hills; Custer County Plains; Pine Ridge Area; Butte County Area; Perkins County; West Central Plains; Ziebach County; Haakon County Area; Badlands Area; Bennett County Area; Northern Campbell; Southern Campbell; Crook County Plains; Weston County Plains; Wyoming Black Hills

details.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT
TONIGHT DUE TO DRY LIGHTNING FOR NORTHERN BLACK HILLS, CENTRAL BLACK
HILLS, SOUTHERN BLACK HILLS, FALL RIVER COUNTY AREA, NORTHERN FOOT
HILLS, EASTERN FOOT HILLS, CUSTER COUNTY PLAINS, PINE RIDGE AREA,
BUTTE COUNTY AREA, PERKINS COUNTY, WEST CENTRAL PLAINS, ZIEBACH
COUNTY, HAAKON COUNTY AREA, BADLANDS AREA, BENNETT COUNTY AREA,
NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, WESTON
COUNTY PLAINS, AND WYOMING BLACK HILLS...

.Thunderstorms expected to develop across northeastern Wyoming into
western South Dakota Saturday afternoon and evening. These storms are
expected to be high based and produce frequent lightning with little
to no rainfall as they move through. The dry storm risk combined with
very hot temperatures in the upper 90s to 100s, very low humidities
of 15 to 20 percent, and dry fuels, critical fire weather conditions
are expected tomorrow afternoon and evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319,
320, 321, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 327, 328, 329, 330, 331, 332,
and 333.

* TIMING...From noon today to midnight MDT tonight.

* LIGHTNING...Frequent dry lightning is possible with thunderstorms.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty and erratic winds are possible in and near
any thunderstorms.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Thunderstorms with little to no rain, gusty and
erratic winds, and frequent lightning are possible.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
details.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
expected. A combination of gusty winds, low relative humidity, and
dry lightning can contribute to extreme fire behavior.

location: Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave; Lake Mead - AZ side; Lake Mohave - AZ side; Northwest Deserts; Death Valley National Park; Western Mojave Desert; Eastern Mojave Desert, Including the Mojave National Preserve; Morongo Basin; Cadiz Basin; San Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley; Northeast Clark County; Western Clark and Southern Nye County; Las Vegas Valley; Southern Clark County; Lake Mead - NV side; Lake Mohave - NV side

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected. Afternoon temperatures
in the desert valleys will climb into the 108 to 114 degree range,
and may exceed 115 along the Colorado River Valley and 120 in Death
Valley. Overnight lows generally 80 to 95 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada including the Greater Mojave Desert region.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.
